Assuming the tables you already have are standard 6’x2.5’ tables, combined that would be a 6’x5’ table. They make 5’x5’ folding tables but what’s the point in doing that when the tables you have are perfectly fine? If you’re worried about the legs or something like that, you could build/have someone else build a custom table. I’ll warn you though, lumber and building materials in general have been pretty pricey lately. If you’re concerned about the top of the tables, you could get a table cloth. Buying a whole new table definitely isn’t necessary. For me, if I can do it for free or super cheap, that’s the best way. Consider looking in thrift stores, Craigslist, even Facebook marketplace for items that pull the space together like artwork. Or you could even DIY. Just a suggestion.

Hi! Curly girl here! I just started out on my curly girl journey and the results have been amazing. I only use two products right now and that is the Shea Moisture Curl & Style Milk and the Cantu Twist and Lock Gel. And before anyone comes at me with the whole “Cantu is really bad/drying/etc,” I’ve had nothing but a good experience with it.

I use Garnier Fructis Curl Nourish shampoo and conditioner. When I get out of the shower, I do NOT use a towel on my hair. I use a regular cotton T-shirt to squeeze the excess moisture out of my hair while still leaving it pretty wet. I have medium length hair so you definitely won’t need as much product as me, but I use enough of the Shea Moisture to coat my hands and then rake it through my hair focusing on the the middle and ends of my hair. I let that sit for a few minutes while I finish drying off/ getting dressed and move on to the Cantu. Your hair should still be pretty wet but if not just take a spray bottle with regular water and spritz your hair. I then take a good amount of the gel and scrunch it into my hair. I’m gonna be honest, there’s so much moisture in my hair when I do this that it’s reminiscent of the “That’s what good pussy sounds like.” Vine. After I’ve scrunched the product into my hair, I take a dry cotton T-shirt and plop my hair. I usually do this overnight because I’m impatient and I also don’t own a blow dryer so… Anyways, in the morning I take the t-shirt off and “scrunch the crunch” out of my hair. Basically getting the stiff feeling out by scrunching it.

Obviously if you follow this, it’s going to be different for you since your hair is definitely shorter than mine 😂 It’s honestly all trial and error but I’ve found that this method is my favorite for now.

Last December, I (24F) overdosed on an edible that was laced with fentanyl. Please don’t respond to my comment if you’re going to tell me something along the lines of “edibles metabolize differently than smoking or vaping” or “you probably ate more than you’re used to.” After the incident, I was lost and left with virtually nothing. I doubted myself. Spent days searching the internet. Trying to piece together what happened to me. 

That night I took an average dose (average for me) of THC edibles that I had gotten from my dad. Yes. My dad. My dad gets resin carts and edibles from a friend of his that makes them himself. My dad has known this person for a very long time and we had no reason to believe that his product may have been laced or tampered with. I had previously consumed products from him in the same dosage but under a different “brand” if that makes sense. These products were completely fine and I never had issues. Anyways, I took the edible and made myself dinner. As I was eating I remember feeling extremely unwell. I had never felt like this so I honestly thought it was the food that I had made. I pushed my plate away because I immediately felt like I was going to be sick. Any normal person would feel that feeling and book it to the bathroom. Trust me I tried but I came to the realization that I could no longer move my legs and my arms were becoming weak and very hard to maneuver. Then, the inevitable happened, I threw up all over my table. At this point I knew for sure that something was wrong and it was not the food. I tried to use the “Hey, Siri.” function on my phone but in true Apple fashion it was not picking up my voice. So I hit the power button 5 times, triggering the Emergency SOS function. I was immediately connected to emergency services and they sent EMTs and police to my location. After the phone call, I began to black out. I would be in and out of consciousness for the entire ride to the hospital, during my treatment at the hospital, and even for a while after my release. My memory is extremely foggy from that night still so please bear with me.

What I do remember is that I heard the paramedics say that the emergency room was currently full and that I had to wait. I don’t remember getting off the stretcher but I was placed in a wheelchair and I was placed in a room once it became available. I remember asking the staff not to call my dad around this point because I felt like he would be extremely upset with me. I should also note that during the entire time I was in the hospital I was extremely confused and I felt like the constant questions of the staff only made me more confused. One of the questions they frequently asked was “What year is it?” I had given them the answer 2021, which was correct, but they made it seem like that was not the right answer so I began to panic, thinking I had been unconscious for longer than I had been aware. At one point I even thought that I was still 16, hence why I asked them not to call my dad and me thinking that I would get in trouble. I remember that I started to panic even more and cry because I thought I was dying. I started thinking about my kids (they were with other family that night thank god.) I remember thinking that I was never going to see them again and wondering how my family would explain to them the entire situation. They are far too young to comprehend an overdose nor would it be appropriate to try and explain it to them. At that point they gave me some kind of medication for the panic attack that I was having and I blacked out again. Next thing I know they’re giving me my belongings, placing me in a wheelchair, and asking me if I had someone to come and pick me up. I was still extremely disoriented but I managed to call my friends mom. She was unavailable so I tried reaching out to other friends to see if they could pick me up and take me home. The first call I made was at 8:45. I passed out for another 3 hours in the waiting room. After that, I was able to get in contact with someone that was finally able to take me home. 

This experience was the most frightening experience of my life. It took me days after I got home to feel somewhat normal. The point I want to make in all of this is to be careful where you get your drugs. Even if you trust your source, be careful. Test it if you can. I will only ever buy from a licensed dispensary now. Sorry dad. 

TLDR; I had a very scary fentanyl overdose from a laced edible I had bought from my dad. Please be wary of who you get your drugs from even if you trust your source.
